newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Avesta Sheffield says tough quarter ahead.
newsitem.headline: Avesta Sheffield says tough quarter ahead.

text.p: Swedish-British steel company Avesta Sheffield AB said on Thursday it expected prices to rise slowly but that the final quarter of its fiscal year ending March 31, 1997, would also be troublesome.
It said in its nine-month results statement that order intake for several of its products was strong in Europe but weak in the U.S..
"The third quarter was a disappointment and the last quarter will also be troublsome," the company said.
"In the current generally uncertain market situation the improvement in earnings will be slow.

"Management attention will mainly be on additional cost cutting with focus on the steel mill in Avesta (Sweden) and operations in North America that have a difficult market situation," the steel company said.
The company reported a pretax loss of 136 million crowns for the first nine months of the year, compared with a pretax profit of 3.15 billion crowns in the corresponding period a year earlier.
In a Reuters poll, analysts expected on average a pre-tax profit of 163 million crowns.

Avesta Sheffield swung to an operating loss after depreciation of 153 million crowns from an operating profit of 3.06 billion, while loss per share amounted to 0.24 crowns, compared with a profit of 13.70 crowns.
Nine-month sales fell to 12.65 billion crowns from 16.60 billion.
The company painted a gloomy picture of the current market situation.
"Despite strong demand for cold rolled products, price increases will be modest and they will also be counterbalanced by currency development in Britain," the company said.
Prices for products made from cold rolled materials, such as pipes, are also under pressure, the company said.
But as of April Avesta Sheffield expects higher prices, following some producers annnouncing price hikes of 7-8 percent.
"Also the price increase on nickel will have some positive effects," the company said.
